jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day You join a team that is being built right now. Transformation of Industry is setting up a dedicated Function Controlling for the first time, and you are part of it from the start. On 25 August 2026 Siemens Energy announced preparations for the legal and operational separation of Transformation of Industry into a standalone company, a fast-growing business with around 17,000 employees, €6 billion of revenue and a double-digit profit margin. A standalone company needs its own transparency on the cost of its central functions — and that is exactly what this team delivers.You begin the day by reviewing the latest forecast for one of TI's central functions. Headcount, external spend and project costs have moved, and the functional leadership team needs a clear view of the financial impact. You discuss the key drivers, challenge assumptions and agree on actions. Later, you prepare the monthly performance review, coordinate inputs with local controllers and work with colleagues on a more efficient reporting solution. You are close to the business, comfortable with detail and able to turn numbers into a concise management message.This is a rare moment to join. A new company is being built, and with it a new Finance organization: the central Business Controlling team of Transformation of Industry is developing into the Corporate FP&A department of that company, an organization of more than 100 finance professionals. Within it, the Function Controlling team is defining common standards for planning, reporting, performance management and allocations — and you help shape them while owning the day-to-day business partnering for your functions. In this position you report directly to the Head of Function ControllingHow You’ll Make an Impact * Act as Finance Business Partner for corporate functions such as IT, HR, Communications, Legal & Compliance, Procurement or Finance, supporting their leaders in financial and performance decisions* Coordinate budgeting, forecasting, monthly closing and mid-term planning for assigned functions, ensuring alignment with local and regional controllers* Analyze cost, headcount, project and resource developments, explain deviations, identify risks and opportunities, and ensure consistent planning, reporting and data quality* Prepare management reports, performance reviews and decision-support materials, and support business cases, investment assessments and ad-hoc analyses for functional initiatives* Challenge spending plans and identify, quantify and track efficiency measures, supporting sound financial decisions and effective resource allocation* Develop allocation, charging and governance concepts, and improve controlling processes through standardization, automation and digital reportingWhat You Bring* A university degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Industrial Engineering or a related field* Longstanding experience in controlling, FP&A, cost controlling, function controlling or finance business partnering, with solid knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, cost center controlling and variance analysis* An analytical and structured approach, combining attention to detail with a clear understanding of the broader business context* A proactive, hands-on attitude and the flexibility to work effectively in a changing organization with a high workload* Strong communication skills and the confidence to challenge assumptions constructively and follow topics through to resolution, combined with good Excel and PowerPoint skills; knowledge of SAP, Power BI, SAC or comparable tools is a plus* Fluent English; additional languages are an asset but not requiredAbout the TeamOur Transformation of Industry division is decarbonizing the industrial sector. Increasing electrification and efficiency are key and demand for green H2 and derivative fuels will rise. We enable decarbonization of the industrial sector and the transition to sustainable processes, building on a strong industrial customer base, a global network, diverse technologies, and integrated execution capabilities.Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.You do not need to tick every box. If this role excites you and you bring most of it, we would like to hear from you.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

You will contribute to timely and accurate safety reporting to regulatory authorities and internal stakeholders, analyze safety data from clinical and post‑market sources, and collaborate cross‑functionally to identify, assess, and mitigate potential safety risks. Your work will play a key role in safeguarding patient well‑being and maintaining compliance with global regulatory standards. product development and post‑market phases to assess safety risks and contribute to the development and implementation of effective risk management strategies.- Conduct scientific literature reviews and ongoing safety surveillance activities to identify new or evolving safety issues and ensure continuous compliance with regulatory standards.- Respond to safety‑related inquiries from healthcare professionals, patients, and internal stakeholders, ensuring transparent, accurate, and professional communication regarding product safety.- Support the implementation and continuous improvement of safety‑related processes, policies, and procedures, and maintain up‑to‑date knowledge of evolving medical device safety regulations and guidelines.You should bring the following- Bachelor’s or meetings.Technical & Functional Skills- Regulatory Compliance- Risk Management and Risk‑Benefit Analysis- Safety Assessment & Surveillance- Adverse Event Reporting and Signal Detection- Safety Data We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly’s operational and analytical systems.This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. Your leadership will help ensure smooth, controlled, and low-risk transitions into the new SAP S/4HANA environment.How You’ll Make an Impact * Own and drive the global SAP S/4HANA cutover strategy, ensuring a controlled, business-ready transition across all rollout waves* Develop and maintain integrated cutover plans covering data migration, system validation, go-live activities, legacy system integration, and decommissioning* Define governance, readiness criteria, key milestones, and decision gates while ensuring all deployment dependencies are managed effectively* Identify cutover risks early, develop contingency and fallback strategies, and lead issue resolution to minimize business disruption during critical go-live periods* Guide and support Cluster Cutover Managers by providing standardized methodologies, coordinating execution, and ensuring alignment with global deployment objectives* Monitor cutover performance through KPIs, status reporting, and governance meetings while providing clear, decision-oriented updates to Program Management and executive stakeholdersWhat You Bring* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Information Technology, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience* Extensive experience leading SAP S/4HANA cutover, deployment, transition, or large-scale ERP transformation programs in complex global environments* Strong expertise in integrated cutover planning, data migration, system validation, go-live management, legacy system integration, and operational readiness* Proven experience in risk management, contingency planning, business continuity, milestone tracking, KPI reporting, and executive-level communication* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and coordinate business stakeholders, global delivery organizations, Cluster Cutover Managers, and external implementation partners* Fluent English is required; German or additional languages relevant to the rollout regions are considered an advantageAbout the TeamIn our Business Functions we enable our organization to reach their targets by providing best-in class services and solutions in the areas of IT, HR, Finance, Real Estate, Strategy & Technology and more. Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs The S4 program at Siemens Energy, formally called S4E or S4E‑Unify, is one of the major global Business- & IT Transformation Programs within Siemens Energy (SE). Its key objective is to transform our historical patchwork of 23 legacy SAP systems into a completely new platform based on the latest state-of-the-art SAP S/4 HANA technology. At the same time, S4E-Unify is aiming for the optimization and harmonization of SE’s worldwide Business Processes across all Business Areas, Regions and Functions. Goal is to significantly reduce complexity, increase speed and flexibility, foster cross-organizational collaboration and finally drive significant cost reductions. The S4E-Unify core team consists of roughly 300 colleagues around the globe plus a substantial extended community of subject matter experts (SME), change network ambassadors and other contributors. It affects 40,000 global users and follows an implementation roadmap through 2030.  The S4E program is delivered through phased “Unify” rollout waves, bringing sites and business areas live step by step on SAP S/4HANA. It includes standardized business templates, a defined operating model with strong governance and board‑level sponsorship, and an enhanced user experience that modernizes how employees work.

jobs.description: Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. increase of 2% per yearNext Steps & How to ApplyPlease apply via our recruitment agency 8bit via https://8bitplay.com/jobs/principal-c-engineer/• A one-hour technical conversation with the Engineering jobs.description: Start your cyber career with us!As part of the global Cybersecurity Assurance function, we help Siemens to achieve their goals by providing objective, factual and independent assurance to the Siemens Managing Board and Audit Committee. As a business partner to Siemens executive management, we leverage our expertise in a wide range of topics to create an impact that drives change. We offer a vibrant and inclusive environment which ensures a variety of perspectives and enables big picture thinking.To deliver on our vision of being pioneers in assurance and a talent incubator for Siemens, we offer a unique Grow and Development Model. We believe in the concept of lifelong learning and therefore encourage our people towards a mindset where continuous upskilling and reskilling becomes a natural part of our career. We invest in our expertise and therefore provide continuous career coaching, trainings and mentoring, all whilst working with top Siemens business leaders on multiple high-profile projects around the world.Our Cybersecurity team provides core assurance over the cybersecurity health of the company which includes IT infrastructures, product security, software development and cloud environments. We are on the lookout for people with a great skillset, an international mindset and new ideas who understand Siemens businesses and how Cybersecurity helps enable and increase market value. Are you one of them?To discover more about the global Siemens assurance function click here (https://assets.new.siemens.com/siemens/assets/api/uuid:832d2c5d-e30c-4163-a1be-9fa3d67f645b/controlling-and-finance-assurance-info-for-applicants.pdf) .What part will you play?- As valuable member of the assurance team you will be responsible for conducting and driving Cybersecurity assessments across the entire Siemens landscape, including products, services, IT-systems, and software development centers. During this process you will plan and perform ethical hacking activities, design attack scenarios for state-of-the-art technologies and highlight important observations to translate technical findings into management information so that they can take effective actions. - Apply advanced hacking principles and red team methodologies, tools and techniques to mimic real-world threat behaviors faced by the Siemens’s digital environment, e.g. cloud applications, on-premise infrastructure, digital products and services.- You work closely with cybersecurity experts from multiple industries to improve their solutions by tackling the root cause of the issues and find innovative solutions to modern challenges.- You independently conduct research on latest developments in cybersecurity technologies and threats and understand how this is impacting and changing the Siemens’ environment.You'll win us over by having the following qualifications:- Strong academic history (Bachelor degree) in IT, Computer Science or other related fields; certifications such as GIAC GPEN, OSCP, OSWE, CRTO, CREST, etc. are a plus. - Good scripting and programming skills and experience with languages such as Bash, Python, Powershell, and C++ / C#.- At least 5+ years of professional full-time working experience within Siemens or a related industry in penetration testing / red teaming with a proven record of continuous career development.- Demonstrated affinity to learn about the latest trends in cybersecurity and keep up to date in a continuously challenging environment.- You have solid experience with one or more of the following aspects of penetration testing / red teaming: application and software security, EDR and antivirus evasion, C2 setup, automation and scaling of security testing, Active Directory attacks, etc.- Demonstrated experience in capture the flag (CTFs) events, bug hunting or vulnerability research (CVEs) is a plus.- Experience with leveraging and integrating AI into day-to-day work is considered an advantage.- Fluent in English. German or other languages are a plus.- You demonstrate an international mindset and are open to international travel, and working in a diverse teamWhile commitment to our job improves performance, growth happens when we stretch beyond our comfort zone. We offer great benefits and rewards, as you'd expect from a world leader in industrial software.We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. At BMW Car IT, a wholly owned subsdiary of BMW AG, we live and breathe software. We design and implement embedded aoftware for electronic control units of the BMW cars as well as related tools and frameworks. By delivering software all the way from the idea to the final product we lead BMW into the future of digitalization and mobility.

What awaits you?

- You ensure system stability for Linux and Android-based embedded platforms across software deliveries.
- You analyse and resolve complex issues related to performance, boot behavior, memory management, CPU load, and system services.
- Furthermore, you debug cross-layer issues across kernel, frameworks, HALs, middleware, drivers, and applications.
- In addition, you perform root cause analysis using tracing, profiling, and debugging tools.
- You examine crash dumps, kernel panics, ANRs, watchdog resets, and memory leaks to improve system robustness.
- Moreover, you develop proof of concepts, validation solutions, and automation tools for analysis and monitoring.
- You collaborate with cross-functional teams and drive continuous improvements in platform reliability and software quality.

What should you bring along?

- University degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, or a comparable field.
- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in Linux and Android embedded systems.
- Extensive experience with Linux kernel, Android framework, system services, boot process, and resource management.
- Advanced knowledge of debugging, tracing, profiling, and performance analysis tools such as GDB, Perf, Ft , Perfetto, ADB, and Logcat.
- Experience in analysing crashes, memory leaks, deadlocks,   conditions, kernel panics, ANRs, and performance bottlenecks.
- Professional experience in embedded software development and quality assurance in the automotive industry.
- Very good business English skills; German language skills are an advantage.

Would you like to improve the stability, reliability, and performance of next-generation automotive platforms in a highly collaborative environment? Apply now!

Note: Please apply exclusively online via our career portal. Applications via other channels (esp. e-mail) cannot be considered.

- Company car option.
- English speaking teams in an intercultural setting.
- Flexible organisation of working times & mobile work arrangements.
- Career development & continuous personal qualification.
- Relocation Services for our new employees.

Earliest starting date: from now on

Working hours: full time

jobs.description: The Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics (WIAS) is an institute of the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. (FVB). The FVB comprises seven non-university research institutes in Berlin which are funded by the federal and state governments. The research institutes belong to the Leibniz Association.WIAS invites applications for aResearch Assistant Position (f/m/d)(Ref. 26/22)in the Research Group “Nonsmooth Variational Problems and Operator Equations”(Head: Prof. Dr. Michael Hintermüller),starting on January 1, 2027.Field of work:The successful candidate will work in the MATH+ project "DOC-TWIN: Duality-Based Error Control for Optimal Control Problems in Digital-Twin-Based Structural Health Monitoring". The project aims at developing a convex-duality-based framework for reliable error control in PDE-constrained optimal control problems motivated by digital-twin-based structural health monitoring.The Tasks include:- Developing and analyzing duality-based a posteriori error identities for PDE-constrained optimal control problems;- Deriving corresponding discrete a priori error identities and using them for convergence-rate analysis and certified nonlinear solver control;- Designing, implementing, and numerically validating finite element methods, including adaptive mesh-refinement strategies and suitable post-processing techniques;- Preparing scientific publications and presenting the results at workshops and conferences.**We are looking for: **Applicants with:- A very good university degree in mathematics, computational science, engineering, or a closely related field;- A strong interest in numerical analysis, optimization, partial differential equations, or scientific computing;- A willingness to work on both the mathematical analysis and the implementation of numerical methods for PDE-constrained optimization problems;- Good communication skills and the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment;- Good written and spoken English skills.Desirable Qualifications:Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage but not a requirement:- Finite element methods, adaptive methods, or a posteriori error estimation;- Convex analysis, nonsmooth optimization, or optimal control;- PDE-constrained optimization or inverse problems;- Numerical methods for elasticity, structural mechanics, or related models;- Implementation of numerical methods in Python, MATLAB, Julia, C/C++, or finite element software.What we offer:- The opportunity to work at WIAS Berlin, a leading research institution with strengths in partial differential equations, mathematical modeling, nonlinear optimization, and applied mathematics in general;- The option of mobile working;- A certified family-friendly work environment (Audit berufundfamilie);- The opportunity to live and work in Berlin, one of the world's most culturally rich and diverse international cities. Berlin offers a wide range of opportunities to enjoy life outside work while remaining relatively affordable compared with other major cities. Neither the position nor living in Berlin requires knowledge of German, although WIAS offers free German courses. We particularly welcome international applicants. Berlin also offers a rich scientific landscape, with numerous research opportunities and career prospects in both academia and industry;- Close mentorship from the supervisor and other peers through a dedicated mentorship program.Please direct scientific queries to Prof Dr. Michael Hintermüller (michael.hintermueller@wias-berlin.de).The appointment is limited to two years. The position is full-time (39 hours per week), with a salary based on pay grade E 13 of the German TVöD Bund pay scale.WIAS is committed to fostering diversity and equal opportunities and particularly encourages women to apply. Applicants with disabilities will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal qualification. If you have any questions or want to provide us with information related to diversity, inclusion or disabilities, please feel free to consult our website orcontact our Diversity Officer, Sara Krummenacher (sara.krummenacher@wias-berlin.de).How to apply:Please upload your complete application documents (motivation letter, detailed CV, certificates, copy of the master thesis, etc.) via our applicant portal using the button “Apply online”.The application period opens immediately and remains open until the position is filled.We are looking forward to your application!

PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application as a single PDF by 19 November 2026, stating the reference number Ref. #11-26021, including:- cover letter describing your motivation to apply for this position- detailed CV- contact details of two potential references- all academic credentials and certificatesPlease submit your application via our online application system. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.If you have any specific questions about the position, please contact Prof. Dr. Thomas Kastner at thomas.kastner@senckenberg.de.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact xxxxx atvorname.nachname@senckenberg.deFor data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.Application documents will also be made available to members of the selection committee from Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE), solely for the purpose of assessing applications and selecting candidates.

jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as soon as possible:PostDoc (m/f/d) in Data-Driven Social Ecological Research(Full-Time / Part-Time** **options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.SBiK-F has strong cooperations with the Institute for social-ecological research (ISOE) and the position will work closely with both institutions.The position develops quantitative approaches to (1) better characterize and measure human–nature interactions, or (2) use these analyses to identify leverage points for more effective stewardship or monitoring of nature under climate change.Your tasks- Develop quantitative approaches to measure and analyze human–nature interactions- Integrate multiple data streams (ecological, social, remote-sensing, citizen-science) into coherent models of social-ecological system dynamics- Identify leverage points where intervention or monitoring most effectively supports biodiversity- Advance biodiversity or stewardship monitoring frameworks to better incorporate social dimensions- Publish in leading international journals- Contribute to and connect with ongoing research at SBiK-F- Collaborate across the natural- and social-science groups at Senckenberg, ISOE, and partner institutionsYour profile- PhD in ecology, environmental science, quantitative social science, or a related field- Demonstrated experience working with empirical ecological data and preferably also social data- Strong proficiency in R (and/or comparable statistical/programming environments)- Excellent quantitative and statistical skills- Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals- Fluency in written and spoken EnglishDesirable skills- Experience with integrating heterogeneous data streams (eg. ecological, social, remote sensing or citizen science data)- Familiarity with AI/ML methods- Track record of interdisciplinary collaboration across natural and social sciences- Experience in quantitative social science methods and working with social or socio-economic data- Experience in acquiring third-party funding- Familiarity with trait-based approaches to social-ecological questions- Familiarity with adaptive capacity and resilience of social-ecological systems- Familiarity with impacts of climate change on the interactions between biodiversity and societyWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. jobs.description: Create your own happiness!Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?What you can look forward to…The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term, but an extension is possible.Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the children (age 1-6) entrusted to us in line with our educational approach, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. In your daily work, you would speak mainly English.We would appreciate at least some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.The Team: One for all, all for one!Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.Has this piqued your curiosity? Then you should definitely keep reading…Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.Feel free to get to know us!The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 42-48 children are currently cared for by nine early childhood educators. Our facilities allow us to organize various projects and activities in workshops and specialized rooms.The foundation of our concept is the Reggio approach. Above all, it reflects our attitude toward others and how we wish to approach life’s changes. Our daycare is a place for self-directed, holistic learning, and we foster a respectful approach not only toward the children entrusted to us, but toward all people.We integrate key areas such as yoga, woodworking, art studio work, language development, music, relaxation and movement, and preschool preparation into our daily routine. Do you have a particular focus? A passion? Let’s find out together if we can integrate this into our daily routine as well…Start up initiative: Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.Our small operator, “Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.”, was founded in 2008 and is a member of the Paritätischer Wohlfahrtsverband Hamburg. Loki Schmidt was the founding patron of our daycare center.Our organization consists of a single facility. This means that decisions can be made and implemented quickly, easily, and on an individual basis. Here, people are still allowed to be people; they are heard and are not just a personnel number.As a member of the Bucerius family and an initiative of the ZEIT STIFTUNG BUCERIUS, our work makes an important contribution to promoting an open, democratic society.The Future: Do you think we’re a good fit for you?Then please send us your application materials. We would love to get to know you.If you’re interested, feel free to check out our website (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita) ) or our Instagram account (kita.buceriuslaw).Thank you for your attention, and we hope to see you soon!

jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.Your tasks- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.Your profile- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Hanieh Saeediat hanieh.saeedi@senckenberg.de

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its institute Senckenberg am Meer, German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research in Hamburg, starting as soon as possibleResearch Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity(full time / part-time )Location: HamburgEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options availableType of contract: temporary contract limited until 30.09.2029Remuneration: collective agreement of the state Hesse, TV-H E13﻿The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.As part of the institute “Senckenberg am Meer” located in Wilhelmshaven, with its two departments Marine Research and German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research (DZMB), the Hamburg research site, which belongs to the DZMB, focuses on researching taxonomy and systematics of marine life forms.The position is based within the Zooplankton Working Group and is part of the joint project ZooM-In (Innovative Methods for National Zooplankton Monitoring), contributing to the further development and standardization of modern methods for marine biodiversity monitoring. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) through the National Biodiversity Monitoring Centre’s initiative Sustainable Biodiversity Monitoring.The project will be carried out in close cooperation with the Helmholtz Institute for Functional Marine Biodiversity (HIFMB) as well as federal and state authorities.Your tasks- Project management of the project ZooM-In- Organisation of and participation in monthly expeditions (March-October, 3-4 days per months) to the North Sea- Organisation of project workshops- Assessment of zooplankton biodiversity by imaging technologies- Cross validation of zooplankton biodiversity assessment by traditional microscopy, molecular genetics and imaging methods- Communication of project results to stakeholders- Publication of project results in peer-reviewed journals- Writing of a project reportYour profile- Master degree in marine biology or natural sciences- Expertise in the application of plankton imaging technologies (ZooScan and/or PlanktoScope)- Relevant knowledge on molecular genetic analyses of organisms, ideally metabarcoding of zooplankton- Experience in data analyses, preferably using R- Experience with sea-going expeditions on research vessels and sampling of plankton, resilience to motion sickness- Willingness to participate in interdisciplinary work- Very good communication skills, ability to work in a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary and international environment- Very good command of English (written and spoken)- Sound command of the German language is essential for this positionWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan- Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) (as a single PDF, max. 10 MB) on our career pagehttps://www.senckenberg.de/de/karriere/ by 8 November 2026.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/.For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.If you have any specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Jasmin Renz at jasmin.renz@senckenberg.de.

The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedElectronics Engineer (m/f/d)Your positionAs an Electronics Engineer, you will support cutting-edge experimental physics research by developing reliable, high-performance electronic systems in close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff.- Develop, design and implement analogue and digital electronic systems for experimental physics applications.- Translate scientific and technical requirements into robust electronic concepts, circuits and complete devices.- Design, assemble, commission and test printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic instruments, from initial concept through prototyping to deployment in the laboratory.- Diagnose, troubleshoot and optimise existing electronic systems and measurement equipment.- Develop firmware for microcontrollers and support the integration of hardware, firmware and software components.- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.Your background and skills- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.Our offer- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.- Opportunities for professional development and further training.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the applicable public-sector collective agreement, depending on qualifications and professional experience.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticketYour applicationThe Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all background.The Max-Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals.To apply please complete the online application form and attach you English CV and motivation letter as well as all relevant certificates latest 15th November, 2026.If you have any questions, please feel free to contact contact Dr. Friedjof Tellkamp by email at friedjof.tellkamp@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:friedjof.tellkamp@mpsd.mpg.de) or Dr. Lars Tiemann at lars.tiemann@mpsd.mpg.de (lars.tiemann@mpsd.mpg.de) .Detailed information about the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter and the online application portal can be found on our website at: https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs (https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs)We look forward to your application.

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years; the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. jobs.description: The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science covering physics, chemistry and biology.23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST – HamburgResearchThe program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. In the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, researchers from the Social Sciences and Humanities as well as artists explore the relationships between technology, science, and society. The Lab was initiated by The Schaufler Foundation together with TUD Dresden University of Technology. The Lab's guiding theme for the upcoming third funding phase (April 2027–September 2030) is "Energy Cultures in Transition". The guiding theme is investigated from a humanities, cultural, social, and educational science perspective, explored through artistic practice, and communicated to the public. For the third funding phase, the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden comprises eight doctoral fellowships and an annually changing Artist in Residence program.TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.The Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden offers, subject to the availability of resources, aDoctoral Fellowshipfor a period of 2 years, with the option of extension by 1.5 years, starting on April 1, 2027. The fellowship (EUR 1,850 per month, plus a grant for material costs of EUR 150 and, where applicable, a family supplement of EUR 315 per child) is aimed at early-career researchers in the field of Sociology. Primary supervision will be provided by Prof. Dr. Susann Wagenknecht, Chair of Micro-Sociology and Technosocial Interaction.The guiding theme Energy Cultures in Transition understands energy as a cultural phenomenon deeply inscribed in aesthetic, historical, political, ecological, economic, and socio-technological practices and systems. Building on the dynamically growing research fields of the Energy Humanities, Science & Technology Studies, and the Digital Humanities, the aim is to examine how modern energy regimes—from petromodernity, to nuclear culture, and post-carbon futures—have shaped not only material infrastructures but also subjectivities, power relations, progress narratives, geopolitical orders, ecologies, and knowledge systems, while simultaneously being shaped by them. Interdisciplinary perspectives from the social sciences, cultural studies, humanities, and educational research represented at the Schaufler Kolleg@TU Dresden enable the analysis of the multifaceted entanglements of energy, culture, and society. The focus is on questions concerning the representation, communication, and aesthetics of energy transitions and resource paradigms as well as continuities between resource economies and information economies, the relationships between energy, labor, environment, and consumer culture, and the role of colonialism, gender, nationalism, geopolitics, education, and social justice in deciding energy futures and navigating collective transformation processes. In the field of Sociology, the following research areas and questions are of particular relevance to the guiding theme:- The (conflict-ridden) negotiation of imaginaries, infrastructures, institutional frameworks, and/or externalities (e.g., emissions, waste, waste heat) associated with energy production and supply across a wide variety of practices, communities, networks, organizations, markets, fields, and/or assemblagesTasks:Your tasks include independent research and academic further qualification with the goal of completing a doctorate at TUD, as well as writing a dissertation on a topic within the guiding concept "Energy Cultures in Transition" in the discipline of Sociology. The fellowship requires a high degree of willingness to engage in interdisciplinary dialogue, particularly with the STEM partnerships of the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, as well as to conduct joint research with artists within the framework of the Schaufler Residency. In addition, engagement in the areas of science communication and outreach is expected. Shared office spaces will be made available to the fellows. Participation in the Kolleg's English-language training program is mandatory.Requirements:You hold an excellent university degree in Sociology or a comparable field in the social sciences, as well as relevant previous experience in the sociological analysis of the environment, technology, or energy, and/or in the field of Science and Technology Studies. You have a strong ability to work in teams and enjoy interdisciplinary collaboration. As the training program is conducted in English, you have English skills at a minimum of C1 level. In accordance with the doctoral regulations of the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Science, the dissertation may be written in either German or English—if you choose to write it in German, corresponding German language skills are required. Beyond this, German language skills are desirable but not mandatoryWe offer:The opportunity to pursue a doctorate within the Schaufler Kolleg with a structured qualification program and integration into an interdisciplinary research project. You will receive a fully equipped office workspace on the premises of TUD and access to an excellent research infrastructure, including participation in Research Studios and writing retreats. The Graduate Academy and other central institutions of TUD offer numerous further training and qualification opportunities. In addition, within the limits of the available project funds, the Schaufler Lab will cover the costs of conference travel. Inclusion and equal opportunities are important to us. We therefore look forward to receiving applications from people regardless of gender, origin, sexual orientation, worldview, or disability. TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The University is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. The focus is on questions concerning the representation, communication, and aesthetics of energy transitions and resource paradigms as well as continuities between resource economies and information economies, the relationships between energy, labor, environment, and consumer culture, and the role of colonialism, gender, nationalism, geopolitics, education, and social justice in deciding energy futures and navigating collective transformation processes. In the field of International Politics, the following research areas and questions are of particular relevance to the guiding theme:- Research on the transnational transition of energy cultures by linking Political Science and International Relations with Social Movement Studies, Sociology, or Conflict Studies- Energy transformation as a political and social distributional conflict in the context of global governance and transnational networks- Challenges of cross-border labour relations in the context of the energy transition, and as objects of analysis for Global Social Policy, Transnational Advocacy Networks, and international norm research- Analysis of legitimation strategies for international objectives (e.g., CO2 reduction) at the national and local levels, particularly in the context of labour- Investigation of global and transnational issues in local contexts, for example through the application of qualitative, comparative, and ethnographic methodsTasks:Your tasks include independent research and academic further qualification with the goal of completing a doctorate at TUD, as well as writing a dissertation on a topic within the guiding concept "Energy Cultures in Transition" in the discipline of Political Science/International Relations/Political Sociology. The fellowship requires a high degree of willingness to engage in interdisciplinary dialogue, particularly with the STEM partnerships of the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, as well as to conduct joint research with artists within the framework of the Schaufler Residency. In addition, engagement in the areas of science communication and outreach is expected. Shared office spaces will be made available to the fellows. Furthermore, you have relevant prior experience in the application of social science methods as well as in the fields of International Politics and Social Movement Studies. You have a strong ability to work in teams and enjoy interdisciplinary collaboration. As the training program is conducted in English, you have English skills at a minimum of C1 level. In accordance with the doctoral regulations of the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Science, the dissertation may be written in either German or English—if you choose to write it in German, corresponding German language skills are required. With a tradition spanning more than 600 years, the Faculty of Medicine at Leipzig University is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With more than 1.300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and provides training for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine and dentistry as well as pharmacy and midwifery. The Faculty of Medicine was founded in 1415, making it one of the oldest medical faculties in Germany with an unbroken tradition of teaching.PhD Position - Craniofacial Biology and PTEN-Dependent Tissue HomeostasisThe research group "Cranio- and Orofacial Development" (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/petersen_lab/) at Leipzig University Medical Center (UKL) offers a PhD position within a DFG-funded collaborative project investigating PTEN-dependent craniofacial tissue homeostasis. The project is particularly suited to candidates interested in craniofacial and skeletal biology, molecular signaling, spatial omics, and metabolism.Project BackgroundPTEN is a central regulator of PI3K-AKT signaling and coordinates cell growth, metabolism, and tissue homeostasis. The project investigates how loss of PTEN in the osteoblast lineage alters the postnatal craniofacial complex. The PhD project will focus on teeth and their supporting periodontal tissues, alveolar and craniofacial bone, and the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Using an inducible postnatal genetic mouse model, we aim to determine how PTEN-dependent signaling changes tissue architecture, bone remodeling, cellular states, and molecular programs.
